title: Allah’s messengers mentioned in the Qur’an
intro: Allah sent a messenger to every people – 25 of them are named in the Qur’an.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Every people had a messenger… <small>(Qur’an, Yunus 10:47, meaning)</small>

Sending messengers is one of the greatest blessings Allah has given to people. Every messenger shows Allah’s mercy to people. The first person on Earth and the first prophet was Adam (AS), and Muhammad (SAW) is the Khatam al-Anbiya’ – the Seal of the Prophets, the last and the best of them. Because messengers are so important for explaining Allah’s revelation, Allah sent a messenger to every people.
Only Allah (SWT) knows the exact number of His messengers. We learned before that the Qur’an mentions 25 by name:

learn.title: Ulul-‘Azm – the messengers of firm resolve
learn.html: Among the most chosen of them are Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, ‘Isa and Muhammad (peace be upon them). Together they are called Ulul-‘Azm – the messengers of firm resolve.
Many ayahs mention the names of Allah’s messengers. A few ayahs in Surah An-Nisa’ and Surah Al-An‘am contain most of them:

learn.title: 📖 An-Nisa’ 4:163–165
learn.html: We sent revelation to you as We sent it to Nuh and the prophets after him; We sent revelation to Ibrahim, Isma‘il, Ishaq, Ya‘qub and his descendants, ‘Isa, Ayyub, Yunus, Harun and Sulayman, and to Dawud We gave the Zabur. Some messengers We have told you about before, and some We have not – and Allah truly spoke to Musa. They were messengers bringing good news and warnings, so that people would have no excuse before Allah after the messengers. Allah is Almighty and Wise. <small>(meaning)</small>

learn.title: 📖 Al-An‘am 6:83–87
learn.html: That was Our proof which We gave Ibrahim against his people. We raise in rank whom We will. We gave him Ishaq and Ya‘qub and guided each of them – and Nuh We guided before – and from his descendants Dawud, Sulayman, Ayyub, Yusuf, Musa and Harun; that is how We reward those who do good. And Zakariyya, Yahya, ‘Isa and Ilyas – all of them were righteous. And Isma‘il, Al-Yasa‘, Yunus and Lut – all of them We favoured above the worlds; and some of their fathers, children and brothers, whom We chose and guided to the straight path. <small>(meaning)</small>
The messengers not named in these two places are mentioned elsewhere in the Qur’an:

items: Adam: He taught Adam the names of all things… (Al-Baqarah 2:31)
Isma‘il, Idris and Dhul-Kifl: all of them were patient. (Al-Anbiya’ 21:85)
Hud and Salih: “O my people, don’t let your disagreement with me bring on you what struck the people of Nuh, or the people of Hud, or the people of Salih…” (Hud 11:89)
Muhammad: Muhammad is only a messenger; messengers have passed away before him. (Al ‘Imran 3:144)

learn.title: Three more chosen servants
learn.html: Besides the messengers, Allah (SWT) also mentions in the Qur’an three of His chosen servants: Luqman, ‘Uzayr and Dhul-Qarnayn.

learn.label: Salawat on the Prophet (SAW)
learn.en: O Allah, send Your blessings on Muhammad.

learn.title: 📜 Hadith
learn.html: “Whoever sends one salawat on me, Allah sends ten blessings on him and writes ten good deeds for him.” (Ahmad)

practice.title: Ulul-‘Azm
practice.prompt: Tap the five messengers of firm resolve (Ulul-‘Azm), then tap Check.

options.why: Yusuf (AS) is a great prophet, but he is not one of the five Ulul-‘Azm.
Luqman is a chosen servant mentioned in the Qur’an, but not one of the 25 named messengers.

questions.q: How many messengers are named in the Qur’an?
Who knows the exact number of all the messengers?
What does the Qur’an call the last Messenger?

options: Ten blessings and ten good deeds

prompts: ❓ What does the Qur’an call the last Messenger of Allah? How many messengers were there in total?
